label: too sparse: rare late-original/delimiter steps in sequences starting with n or 0
explanation: Fires on only 23 of 1M sequences (8 on dev), one activation each, with a narrow magnitude range (0.10-0.13, max 0.130). Every dev activation is in a sequence whose first original token is n or 0. It fires only in the original phase or on the <DEL> step, never in the copy phase. In 0-initial sequences it fires at or just before <DEL>, usually right after a z (e.g. 0 r s 1 w m 0 z [<DEL>]). In n-initial sequences it fires mid-original, usually right after an m (e.g. n m m [s]). These conditions are far too common to be the explanation: the best disjunction gets precision ~0.002 on dev, so most matching steps do not activate. Too few examples to find a predicate; the predicate is a weak descriptive placeholder.
